newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: MMI Holdings seeks to diversify customer base.
newsitem.headline: MMI Holdings seeks to diversify customer base.

text.p: Singapore Hard disk drive maker MMI Holdings Ltd (MMI) will diversify its customer base and products to spread the risk of over-dependency, managing director and co-founder Teh Bong Lim said on Wednesday.
"Our dependence on Seagate has been declining," he said. "This shows the company has taken steps to diversify its customer base."

Teh said Seagate Technology, the world's largest independent disk drive maker, now accounted for 86 percent of sales and about 88 percent of MMI's earnings. Seagate accounted for nearly 100 percent of MMI's sales in 1994 and 1995.
Other customers include MKE and Toshiba, and Creative Technology, for which it assembles multimedia products.
Teh said it was not unusual for a disk drive manufacturer to rely heavily on one customer when more than 80 percent of the market was dominated by five major players.
"Our relationship with Seagate is one of vertical integration into the manufacturing and product development processes," Teh said. He said MMI would look for more such strategic alliances.
The group would decided in nine to 12 months whether to set up facilities in China to penetrate a new market and to be closer to Seagate plants, he added.
Teh said MMI had recently forged alliances with Japanese companies such as Matsushita-Kotobuki Electronics.
"We've been attempting to break into the Japanese market, but on our own we were unsuccessful," Teh said. He said the alliances had enabled MMI to secure new disk drive customers.
He said the group's growth strategy was to focus on its core business in hard disk drive manufacturing and to develop niche segments.
Products range from baseplates, actuator arms, disk clamps, covers and voice coil motors.
MMI has factories in Penang and Johore, Malaysia, which are engaged in precision die-casting, cleanroom assembly of electronic components and printed circuit board assembly.
On Wednesday, MMI offered 76.8 million shares at Singapore $0.52 each in its initial public offering on the main board of the Stock Exchange of Singapore.
It said it hoped to raise net proceeds of S$30.4 million to be used to buy a factory in Malaysia and an office building in Singapore.
Proceeds would also be used to buy more machinery, repay bank borrowings and for working capital.
For the financial year ended June 30, 1996, MMI made a net profit of S$5.11 million on a turnover of S$90.07 million.
Teh said the target for 1997 was S$113 million on a turnover of around S$8.1 million.
